mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior six-month average signals stronger household demand, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0.3% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market that increases wage pressure, which in turn boosts corporate margins and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive excess return over baseline in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior 12-month average signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% combined with a monthly increase in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS) above 0.3% signals a tightening labor market with rising wage pressure, which boosts corporate margins and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND PAYEMS > 0.3% in the same month
regime_hint: tight labor market with rising wage pressure
failure_condition: No significant positive excess return over baseline in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below the prior 12-month average combined with a monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the prior 12-month average signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-month moving average AND HOUST < 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above the prior 12-month average combined with a monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior 12-month average signals strengthening manufacturing activity and demand, which boosts earnings growth and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 > 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive excess return over baseline in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).
